entities.name: Demetrios Chrysoloras
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Demetrios Chrysoloras was a Byzantine politician and writer who served under emperors Manuel II Palaiologos and John VII Palaiologos.

Born in the late 14th century, Chrysoloras rose to prominence as a diplomat and administrator, playing a crucial role in the Byzantine Empire's relations with the Ottoman Empire.

He was instrumental in negotiating the Treaty of Constantinople in 1403, which marked a significant turning point in the empire's decline.

Chrysoloras's legacy extends beyond his political achievements, as he was also a prolific writer and scholar, leaving behind a body of work that continues to be studied by historians today.

Despite his importance, Chrysoloras remains somewhat of a shadow figure in historical records, overshadowed by the more famous figures of his time.

The 2020 discovery of a previously unknown manuscript attributed to Chrysoloras shed new light on his life and work, providing a fascinating glimpse into the world of 15th-century Byzantine politics and culture.
